title: Telegraf
description: The Telegraf instances: WLC telemetry (gRPC dial-out on mon01/02 behind the monitoring VIP), the pvestatd listener and fw-wan's VyOS Telegraf. Health tiles from the alert rules, listeners, inputs, outputs, the series they export, process stats.

panels.title: Checks
panels.description: The Telegraf alert rules, as tiles: WlcTelemetryStopped (no cisco_telemetry_mdt metrics for 10 min), WlcTelemetryWriteDropping (an output of the WLC Telegraf dropped metrics in 15 min: buffer full), WlcTelemetryNotInPrometheus (no wlc_client_live_run_state_clients in job wlc), PveMetricsStopped, PveMetricsAuthFailing (pvestatd writes with a wrong token), TargetDown for the four jobs and MonitoringVIPNotHeldOnce (10.5.11.102). 'receiver = VIP holder' has no alert: the Telegraf that receives the WLCs' stream must be the one on the VIP holder (the WLCs only reach the VIP).

targets.expr: (count(sum by (host) (rate(internal_gather_metrics_gathered{job="telegraf", input="cisco_telemetry_mdt"}[10m])) > 0 and on (host) node_network_address_info{job="node", role="monitoring", address="10.5.11.102"}) or vector(0)) == bool 1

panels.title: WLC receiver (VIP holder)
panels.description: The mon holding the monitoring VIP 10.5.11.102, where the WLCs dial out to: its Telegraf gets the whole gRPC stream, the other one idles. The wlc job scrapes the backend VIP, so it lands there too.

panels.title: WLCs reporting
panels.description: C9800s whose live client count (pushed every 30 s whether or not there are clients) is in job wlc right now: 2 = both wlc-1 and wlc-2 stream.

panels.title: PVE nodes reporting
panels.description: Proxmox nodes whose pvestatd pushes reach the pvestatd Telegraf (7 in the lylat cluster + greatfox, which is often powered off on purpose).

panels.title: Gather errors (1 h)
panels.description: Failed gathers of every input on every Telegraf in the last hour. fw-wan's chrony input fails on every interval (it times out after 10 s; see Inputs), so this is rarely 0.

panels.title: Samples per scrape
panels.description: What each job hands to Prometheus per scrape (summed over its targets). telegraf = WLC telemetry Telegraf on mon01/02, pvestatd = Proxmox metric-server Telegraf (the elected replica's container, host "pvestatd"), vyos-telegraf = fw-wan's VyOS Telegraf. wlc = the WLC telemetry itself.

panels.title: Instances
panels.description: One row per Telegraf process. telegraf = WLC telemetry Telegraf on mon01/02, pvestatd = Proxmox metric-server Telegraf (the elected replica's container, host "pvestatd"), vyos-telegraf = fw-wan's VyOS Telegraf. Started: since the process started (a reload keeps it). Buffer max: the fullest output buffer against its metric_buffer_limit (200 000 on the WLC Telegraf, 10 000 elsewhere); at 100 % the oldest metrics are dropped. Series: samples per scrape of its own /metrics (for pvestatd that is all pvestatd_* series).

panels.title: Monitoring VIP holder
panels.description: Which mon held 10.5.11.102 when. A keepalived failover moves the WLCs' gRPC stream (they reconnect within a push interval or two) and the wlc job's scrape target with it.

targets.expr: max by (host) (node_network_address_info{job="node", role="monitoring", address="10.5.11.102"}) or max by (host) (up{job="telegraf"}) * 0

panels.title: Telemetry received per Telegraf
panels.description: Metrics per second from the gRPC dial-out (one metric per YANG list entry per push). Only the VIP holder should show traffic; 0 for 10 min fires WlcTelemetryStopped.

panels.title: gRPC stream errors
panels.description: cisco_telemetry_mdt errors: a WLC's stream ended ('receive error during GRPC dialout ... context canceled' on a Telegraf reload, or the WLC dropped/reconnected). Isolated bursts at reloads are normal; a steady rate means a WLC keeps reconnecting (see Logs).

panels.title: wlc_* series per WLC
panels.description: Series in job wlc per controller, and the samples per scrape of the :9275 endpoint. Telegraf expires a series 150 s after its last push; a WLC dropping out, or whole subscriptions missing, shows as a step down. The controller with the AP and clients carries most of them.

panels.title: wlc_* metric families
panels.description: The 15 largest wlc_* names by series count (one per YANG path and numeric field, see telegraf/wlc.star). The *_info series carry the strings as labels.

panels.title: Clone and Starlark (wlc.star)
panels.description: Every telemetry metric is cloned to wlc_* and reshaped by wlc.star before the :9275 output: processor errors (a Starlark exception drops the metric) and what reaches that output per second. Received but not here = the processing broke (WlcTelemetryNotInPrometheus).

panels.title: HTTP requests
panels.description: Requests to :8186 per second: one write per PVE node per pvestatd cycle (~10 s), so ~0.8/s with 8 nodes. Health checks are the deploy's curl; 404s are clients on a wrong path. This is the elected replica's container only (Mimir keeps one copy of the pair).

panels.title: Rejected writes (wrong token)
panels.description: Writes refused with 401: a PVE metric-server entry (pvestatd-<backend> in /etc/pve/status.cfg) with a token that isn't pvestatd_token. Alert PveMetricsAuthFailing.

panels.title: Metrics received / PVE nodes
panels.description: pvestatd_* metrics per second (one per node, guest, storage, disk and NIC per push) and the nodes in them. 0 for 10 min fires PveMetricsStopped. A greatfox gap is expected (often powered off).

panels.title: pvestatd_* series by object
panels.description: Series in job pvestatd per pvestatd object type (qemu dominates: per VM disk and NIC). Each series expires 60 s after its last push (a stopped guest drops out).

panels.title: pvestatd_* series per node / guest
panels.description: The 15 objects with the most pvestatd_* series: PVE nodes (per-CPU, per-NIC) and VMs with many disks/NICs.

panels.title: Metrics gathered per input
panels.description: Metrics per second each input produced (Telegraf's own internal input left out). Listener inputs (cisco_telemetry_mdt, influxdb_v2_listener) count what was pushed to them; the rest are polled every agent interval.

panels.title: Gather errors per input
panels.description: Failed gathers per input. fw-wan's chrony input fails every interval (each attempt runs into the 10 s timeout, see Gather time); cisco_telemetry_mdt errors are WLC streams ending.

panels.title: Gather time per input
panels.description: How long each polled input's last collection took (listeners don't gather, left out). Close to the agent interval means the input can't keep up; 10 s flat is a timeout (fw-wan chrony).

panels.title: Processor and parser errors
panels.description: Processors: clone + starlark (WLC), rename/enum/starlark/converter (pvestatd). Parser: fw-wan's exec inputs. Startup: an input that failed to start and is being retried.

defaults.noValue: No processor, parser or startup errors in range

panels.title: Metrics written per output
panels.description: Per second. prometheus_client 'writes' into its own cache, which Prometheus scrapes (alias wlc = the :9275 wlc_* endpoint, no alias = Telegraf's internal_* / fw-wan's metrics). Before 2026-11-14 the WLC Telegraf also had influxdb_v2 outputs (alias = the backend whose InfluxDB it wrote to).

panels.title: Dropped, rejected and failed writes
panels.description: Dropped: the buffer overflowed (WlcTelemetryWriteDropping on the WLC Telegraf). Rejected: the output refused the metric (e.g. a name it can't serialize). Write errors: a flush failed and is retried.

defaults.noValue: Nothing dropped, rejected or failed in range

panels.title: Buffer fill per output
panels.description: Metrics waiting in each output's buffer against metric_buffer_limit. The prometheus_client outputs only buffer between flushes, so anything above a few percent means Telegraf can't keep up.

targets.expr: max by (host, output, alias) (internal_write_buffer_size{job=~"telegraf|pvestatd|vyos-telegraf", host=~"$host"} / internal_write_buffer_limit{job=~"telegraf|pvestatd|vyos-telegraf", host=~"$host"})

panels.title: Write time per output
panels.description: How long the last flush of each output took (mean over the interval). prometheus_client flushes into its own cache and takes milliseconds; seconds mean Telegraf is starved of CPU.

panels.title: Samples per scrape
panels.description: Series each target exposes per scrape: pvestatd (every PVE node, guest and storage), fw-wan's Telegraf (after dropping syslog_*), the wlc_* endpoint and the two WLC Telegrafs' own internal_* metrics.

panels.title: New series per hour (churn)
panels.description: Series that appeared for the first time in each scrape, summed over the last hour. Steady churn is labels that keep changing (wlc_*_info strings, guest tags); a spike is a restart or a new device.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: Time to scrape each endpoint (pvestatd every 10 s, the rest at the global interval).

panels.title: Series in Mimir per job
panels.description: Active series in Mimir now, per job (incl. up/scrape_* and, for vyos-telegraf, fw-wan's whole metric set). telegraf = WLC telemetry Telegraf on mon01/02, pvestatd = Proxmox metric-server Telegraf (the elected replica's container, host "pvestatd"), vyos-telegraf = fw-wan's VyOS Telegraf.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores used by each Telegraf.

panels.title: Resident memory
panels.description: RSS. The WLC Telegraf on the VIP holder holds the decoded telemetry and both output caches.

panels.title: Go heap in use
panels.description: Telegraf's own heap figure (internal input); grows with buffered metrics.

panels.title: Goroutines
panels.description: Rises with open gRPC streams and HTTP connections.

panels.title: Errors and warnings per host
panels.description: Telegraf's E! and W! lines (Podman logs them all at priority err, so the journal level means nothing).

panels.title: Telegraf errors and warnings
panels.description: mon01/02 (containers telegraf and pvestatd, journal via Alloy) and fw-wan's telegraf if it logs.
